Findings: (1) Defaults - test strips revision_number/option_ids from q93/q95 via a temp file built from the real fixture (decoder.UseNumber, in-place map mutation, re-marshal), then asserts Revision.Number==1 and positional option id 'lotr-rk-95-opt-4'; this matches import.go's literal defaulting logic (revisionNumber:=1 at L173; oid fallback 'qid-opt-i+1' at L225). (2) Retained option5/answer identity - after re-adding revision_number:2 and q95 option_ids [...opt-1,2,3,5], the test asserts CorrectOptionID=='lotr-rk-95-opt-2', matching the real fixture's correct_answer:1 pointing at option_ids[1]; confirmed against the actual committed JSON (lines 1435-1458) and manifest.json, whose lotr-rk-95 entry already has exactly this opt-1/2/3/5 mapping with source_sha256 equal to the verification.json 'verified_raw_sha256' (case differs only in hex casing). (3) Revision 2 for both q93/q95 - asserted directly, consistent with explicit revision_number handling. (4) 98 non-target objects/mappings - loop asserts reflect.DeepEqual on Draft.Questions and Manifest.Questions for all non-target indices, with an explicit unchanged==98 count; index alignment holds because question order is never reordered, only two map values are mutated in place before marshal. (5) Malformed inputs - the 12 subtests (option_ids null/wrong-type/wrong-length/duplicate/blank/illegal; revision_number null/wrong-type/zero/negative/fractional/overflow) each map cleanly onto concrete branches in import.go (type assertion failures, len mismatch, seenOptionIDs/idPattern checks, integer() json.Number.Int64() failure modes, number<=0 guard), and Code(err) checks the right error kind. Limits of this review: read-only, no test execution performed by me - I verified logic by static inspection of import.go/types.go against the fixture bytes, not by running go test; I could not locate the shared 'legacyBase' fixture and 'importText' helper used by the malformed-values subtests (no grep/glob/bash tool available in this session) so I could not independently confirm that fixture has exactly one '"correct_answer":2' occurrence and 4 options matching the 'question-two-opt-*' ids in the subtest table - this is inferred, not directly observed. worker/verification.json's reported go test pass and root-full-go-checks.json's full-suite pass are reported execution evidence from the submitter/root, not something I re-ran or independently witnessed. Given the directly observable evidence (source code logic, real fixture bytes, manifest bytes) is internally consistent and the test's assertions are meaningful (not tautological), I accept this change. Publication remains a separate later gate per the task's own stated limitations.
